meta.title: DeBERTa Comparison + Data Reuse Plan
meta.description: Head-to-head control eval, training-data harvest, and the data strategy that falls out of measuring train_v8

props.title: DeBERTa comparison + data reuse plan
props.subtitle: Test the incumbent on single commands, harvest its training data, extract the strategy

props.content: Only one DeBERTa is real: the deployed, DVC-pinned model. Every versioned folder is a metadata shell with no weights. Its 100k-row training set is perfectly uniform, template-stamped, and contains zero compound transmissions — which is exactly why the splitter gap exists. The plan: run the pinned model as a diagnostic control against the new stage-2 parser, convert its screened data into intent breadth plus a constituent pool for compound composition, and spend future data budget on template diversity instead of row volume.

props.title: The contestant is forced
props.content: The head-to-head runs against the deployed pinned model because it is the only DeBERTa with weights on disk. v33 through v44c are tokenizer-and-config snapshots only.

props.title: The data is worth harvesting
props.content: train_v8 is 100,000 clean, BIO-aligned atomic rows across 50 intents. Screened, it fills the stage-2 parser's intent-coverage gap and doubles as a constituent pool that satisfies the trainer's aligner by construction.

props.title: The strategy writes itself
props.content: Compounds must be composed, never mined — no existing corpus supplies honest cut-lines. Diversity of phrasing beats volume: 220 templates copied ~455 times each is a memorization engine, not a curriculum.

rows: deberta-v3-large joint intent+slot, hidden 1024; verified runnable on MPS ~185ms/row (2026-07-06)
Metadata-only snapshots; all share one label mapping that does not match the live model

props.title: Head-to-head contestant
props.content: The deployed DVC-pinned model is the incumbent for the comparison. No retrain of any snapshot line is in scope; the snapshots exist as lineage context only.

props.title: eval_curated_v2 is not free to use
props.content: The 4,766-row curated eval set is scenario-derived (ids name real training scenarios). It enters the head-to-head only after exam-lineage screening and char-span to BIO conversion, and its screen verdict gets reported with the results.

props.title: A — head-to-head on single commands
props.content: Deployed pinned DeBERTa vs the SPM stage-2 parser, POC-local, through the existing runtime adapter — no new production call sites, no profile flags, never a promotion. Eval sets: generated AtomicATC test (lineage-separated by construction), screened eval_curated_v2, and exam single-command rows as the realism slice reported by exposure stratum. Label spaces reconcile through production intent names with explicit out-of-vocabulary counts. Metrics: intent accuracy, span slot-F1, per-intent recall, latency. Purpose: calibrate whether stage-2 meets the incumbent's ceiling on atomics before spending on scale-up.

props.title: B — retrain stage-2 with the DeBERTa data
props.content: Convert train_v8 to AtomicATC blocks (labels are already token-aligned, so conversion is near-mechanical) behind the same admission screen as the legacy converter: normalized-utterance vs exam, BATC seal, duplicate and placeholder rejection, rejects logged. The screened atomics play two roles: intent breadth for stage-2 (50 intents vs our 22 receipted families) and a constituent pool for compound composition — compounds built from pool members automatically satisfy the aligner because their constituents exist in AtomicATC. Our FAA-receipted generator stays the only cut-line authority. Dev and test remain ours, never DeBERTa-synthetic.

props.title: C — data strategy from the patterns
props.content: Compose compounds, never mine them. Hold training near-uniform per intent but weight evaluation by exam frequency alongside unweighted scores. Spend the next generation wave on template and connector diversity, not more copies. Repair the starved tails: SPEED, DISTANCE, TIME slots and the twelve exam-frequent intents missing from generator v1 — informational, sequencing, acknowledgment, taxi instruction, verification request, unable response, VFR instruction, comm request, landing clearance, hold short, radar identification, route amendment. Same-intent adjacency stays a small family near 5% — measured rare in the exam at 10 pairs across 438 compound rows.

items.title: Generator v2 with the aligner fix
items.description: Twelve new intent families plus the small amendment family; every mixed block's constituents emitted into the same AtomicATC split, with an alignment-coverage test at 99% or better. This repairs the micro-pilot crash root cause: v1 compounds had no constituents in AtomicATC, so every block was excluded and the train set came up empty.
